title: Seattle Bookshops, Breakfast with Victor, Night Train
summary: Bags into storage, breakfast with Victor, a bookshop crawl north to UW, then the 6pm train.

segments.name: Segment 1 — Bags to the Hyatt House, breakfast with Victor
segments.blurb: Check out, bags up to 5th Ave N, walk down to Ludi's.

stops.name: Airbnb, 425 Vine St
stops.note: Belltown. Check out and carry the bags north.

expect.arrive: Hyatt House is a short walk up from Vine St; the drop takes two minutes, then it is downhill all the way to Ludi's.

paths.do: Four blocks up 5th Ave with the bags, then 1.4km back down through Belltown to Stewart St.
Short Uber from the Airbnb to the Hyatt House if the bags are heavy, then walk to Ludi's.

segments.seasonal: Ludi's is open Monday 7:00am-2:30pm (Yelp listing, read 2026-10-05), so 8:30am is comfortably inside service. The Airbnb and the Hyatt House are both on 5th, four blocks apart — a five-minute walk even with the bags. The Hyatt House down to Stewart St is a longer 1.4km, about 18 minutes downhill, so leave by 8:10am.

segments.name: Segment 2 — Pike Place in short order, Post Alley books
segments.blurb: Five-minute walk from Ludi's. Photos and chowder only.

stops.name: Original Starbucks
stops.note: 1912 Pike Pl. Queue is for the photo, not coffee.

stops.name: Pike Place Market
stops.note: Second pass, photos only — cheese and bao done 4 Oct.

stops.name: Lion Heart Book Store
stops.note: Tiny used bookshop down in the Market's lower levels.

expect.arrive: Five minutes on foot from Ludi's; the market is mid-busy by 10am and the Starbucks queue is already down the block.

paths.do: Starbucks storefront photo, one pass through the arcades, then join the chowder queue at 11:00 sharp.
Left Bank Books at 10am, Lion Heart down in the lower levels, then chowder at 11:00.

segments.seasonal: Pike Place Chowder opens 11:00am Monday and the queue builds fast — being there at opening is the difference between five minutes and forty. Left Bank Books opens 10:00am Mon-Sat; Lion Heart keeps looser hours, so treat it as a bonus.

segments.name: Segment 3 — Book crawl north by Link, UW libraries, the Cut
segments.blurb: One light rail line links every remaining stop.

stops.name: Elliott Bay Book Company
stops.note: 1521 10th Ave. The big one — cedar shelves, 150k titles.

stops.name: Ada's Technical Books
stops.note: 425 15th Ave E. Science and maths, cafe at the back.

stops.name: Magus Books
stops.note: 1408 NE 42nd St. Used stacks, beside U District station.

stops.name: University Book Store
stops.note: 4326 University Way. Four floors on the Ave.

stops.name: Suzzallo and Allen Libraries
stops.note: Collegiate Gothic Reading Room, open to the public.

stops.name: Montlake Cut
stops.note: Ship canal channel; walk the Montlake Bridge span.

stops.name: Washington Park Arboretum
stops.note: Free and open daily — stands in for the Japanese Garden.

expect.arrive: Link from Westlake runs Capitol Hill to U District in under ten minutes; every stop here is a short walk from a station.

paths.do: Every book stop and Suzzallo are indoors; skip the Cut and the Arboretum, Link back downtown for the Central Library instead.
Skip Capitol Hill, Link straight to U District for Suzzallo, Magus, then Montlake Cut.
Elliott Bay and Ada's on Capitol Hill, Link north for Magus and University Book Store, Suzzallo, then walk to the Cut.
As above, then cross Montlake Bridge into the Arboretum for a short Azalea Way stroll before heading back.

segments.seasonal: The Seattle Japanese Garden is CLOSED Mondays (Tue-Sun 10am-5pm from 1 October, seattlejapanesegarden.org, read 2026-10-05) — the Arboretum next door is free and open daily, so that is the substitute. Suzzallo Reading Room is Monday 8am-8pm in autumn quarter, with seismic and facade work running through Fall 2026, so expect scaffolding outside. Elliott Bay opens 9am Monday, Magus 10am. Both UW museums are shut on Mondays (Burke Tue-Sun, Henry Thu-Sun), so the wet-weather fallback is downtown, not on campus.
segments.cost: Link light rail is about $2.25-3.00 USD per ride, or a $8 day pass if you ride more than three times. Suzzallo, Montlake Cut and the Arboretum are all free.

segments.name: Segment 4 — Central Library if it rains, bags, the 6:00pm train
segments.blurb: Indoor backup downtown, then bags by 4pm.

stops.name: Seattle Central Library
stops.note: Koolhaas glass ziggurat. Books Spiral, 10th-floor reading room.

stops.name: Hyatt House Seattle Downtown
stops.note: 4:00pm luggage pickup. Don't cut this closer.

stops.name: Pacific Central Station, Vancouver
stops.note: Arrive 10:00pm; Canadian border check on arrival.

expect.arrive: Montlake back to the Hyatt House is 15 minutes by rideshare in light traffic; the library is three blocks from Symphony station.
expect.need: 30 min to collect bags and reach the station

paths.do: Link from U District to Symphony station, 30 min inside the Central Library, then rideshare up to the bags.
Uber Montlake to the Hyatt House, collect bags, second Uber straight to King Street Station.
Bus 48 then 8 across to Uptown, collect bags, then Uber to the station door.

segments.seasonal: Seattle Central Library is open Monday 10am-6pm and free (spl.org, read 2026-10-05) - the best wet-weather hour in the city and a fair match for Suzzallo. Leave Montlake by 3:30pm — the 4:00pm bag pickup is the hard pin of the day, and afternoon traffic between Montlake and Uptown only gets worse after 4. Amtrak asks for 45 minutes before departure to check bags, so 4:30pm at the station is right. Canadian customs happens on arrival at Pacific Central around 10:00pm, not before boarding.
segments.cost: Central Library is free, no ticket or booking.
